texts: An ICD pocket infection with an exposed generator, after oral antibiotics have failed, needs complete removal of the system, the generator and all the leads, with a new system implanted later on the other side.
Erosion means the whole system is infected, including the leads inside the veins and the heart.
Leaving the old leads, or changing only the generator, gives a high rate of relapse and of lead endocarditis.
After the system is removed and the infection treated, a new device is placed on the opposite side, away from the infected pocket.
Reclosing the wound with long-term antibiotics, or washing the pocket and putting in a new generator, fails.
In the picture, Franky pulls the box and all its wires out together, and a new bodyguard waits on the far side beside an hourglass.
Memory hook: grapes on the wires: out with the box and every wire.
